Subject: Request: customer-scoped retention exception and evidence package

Hi Marissa,

Following up from our security questionnaire (SIG section on data lifecycle) — Novacare needs a customer-scoped clarification for tenant-level log retention and proof-of-delete artifacts. Specific asks from our security and compliance teams: 

- Canonical excerpt from your retention policy describing default TTLs for inference/session logs, debugging traces, and audit logs (including distinctions between hosted vs dedicated/private deployments).
- A sample proof-of-delete for a single tenant (manifest or deletion job output) showing the sequence: mark-for-delete -> compaction -> object removal.
- A small redacted audit-log extract that shows the deletion job execution and resulting S3/obj lifecycle events for a tenant window (we only need a ~3-7 day sample).
- CAIQ/SIG mapping summary for controls related to LOG-RETENTION and DATA-DISPOSAL (high level is fine; procurement may request more later).

We understand some of this is sensitive; please indicate what you can provide via your secure evidence portal vs what requires an NDA/procurement path. Our timeline is: initial evidence needed by Aug 7 to feed our internal SIG review.

Thanks — appreciate a quick scope so we can route internally.

Best,
Alicia Gomez
Director, Information Security
Novacare Health

Option A (sample pack) timeline: 3-5 business days.
Option B (compliance bundle with CAIQ mapping) timeline: 8-12 business days.

We can start with Option A and add the CAIQ mapping once procurement signals they need it. Ben (cc) will provide the technical deletion flow and sample manifest.

Hi Alicia / Marissa — quick technical note on how we handle ephemeral inference/session logs and how we generate the proof-of-delete manifest: 

- Default windows: hosted tenants: session traces and ephemeral request logs are retained for 30 days by default; audit logs (control-plane events) are retained 365 days. Dedicated/private deployments are configurable per contract; we document those TTLs in the retention excerpt.

- Deletion workflow (high level):
  1) Records are marked expired in the TTL index (logical delete flag + tombstone record).
  2) Background compaction job consolidates KV shards and emits object-level delete manifests into internal S3 prefix: s3://retention-manifests/deleted/YYYYMMDD/<tenant-id>/manifest.csv
  3) Objects are moved to a deleted/ prefix and lifecycle rules remove physical objects after a short staging window (7 days) to allow recovery if legal hold requested.
  4) Final purge logs and job events are captured to our audit stream (immutable, append-only).

- Proof-of-delete artifact we can provide: a CSV manifest row per object showing object_key, sha256_hash, deleted_at (ISO), deletion_job_id. We also include the deletion job run log (job id, start/end, return codes).

- For tenants under legal hold we can support a temporary retention variance (e.g., 90 days) with restricted access; however this requires approval from procurement + a signed retention addendum so we can record it in billing/entitlement and enable restricted audit access.

I will assemble a sample manifest and a redacted audit extract for the date range you requested and hand to Marissa for delivery.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

We redacted tenant identifiers and any embedded PII; hashes are included so you can validate integrity. If you need verbatim chain-of-custody for legal review let us know and we will escalate to procurement for the retention addendum and DocuSign.

What we provided (attachments and portal delivery):
- redwood_retention_policy_excerpt.pdf — canonical excerpt for hosted vs dedicated TTLs.
- sample_proof_of_delete_manifest.csv — 12-row sample manifest (object_key, sha256_hash, deleted_at, deletion_job_id). SHA256 manifest hash: 3f7a9b2d4c1e6a8d9b7c4f2a1e6d5f3c2b9a8e7d6c5b4a3f2e1d0c9b8a7f6e5d
- deletion_job_config.yaml — job definition and lifecycle configuration (redacted internal endpoints).
- audit_log_extract_20260728-20260801.csv — redacted audit events showing job start/finish and S3 lifecycle transitions.
- caiq_mapping_summary.xlsx — high-level mapping of CAIQ controls to Redwood artifacts (answers + pointers to evidence).

Evidence portal link: https://evidence.redwoodinference.com/portal/novacare/DN-2026-1345
DocuSign (retention addendum): https://app.docusign.com/novacare/retention-addendum

Next steps we recommend:
1) You and your security team review the sample pack and confirm whether you need the extended CAIQ + SOC 2 control excerpts (Option B).
2) If you need a tenant-specific legal-hold variance (90d), have procurement sign the retention addendum and we will enable the variance and provide full chain-of-custody logs.

Happy to run a quick walk-through with Ben and me if your team wants to review the artifacts live — I can set a 30-min call as early as tomorrow.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Customer Compliance
Redwood Inference
